title: Accounts Receivable KPIs and Collection Reports That Work
summary: The AR KPIs and collection report formats finance leaders need weekly and monthly, including DSO, CEI and aging, and how to automate them across entities.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Many AR teams, even after moving to a modern ERP, still lack proper weekly and monthly collection reports. Figures get pulled into spreadsheets when someone asks. A strong AR reporting pack tracks a small set of KPIs: DSO, collection effectiveness index (CEI), collections vs target, overdue percentage, aging distribution, disputed balance, promise-to-pay kept rate and doubtful debt. Each one is split by entity, country and collector. The weekly report drives action. The monthly report drives management review. Both should refresh automatically from the ERP, not be rebuilt by hand.


## Why Do So Many AR Teams Lack Proper Collection Reports?


It is surprisingly common. A company completes a major ERP migration, often to SAP S/4HANA, Oracle or Dynamics 365. The ledgers are clean, the invoices are correct, and yet the credit team still cannot produce a simple weekly collection report without exporting data into Excel.


In a recent Peakflo discovery call, a credit controller at a multi-entity manufacturer said this directly. They wanted proper collection reports, monthly and weekly, because their system did not provide them ready to use. They had migrated to SAP only recently, and collections reporting had not been part of the core project scope.


ERP implementations focus on transactions: posting invoices, recording receipts and closing periods. Management reporting for collections is usually treated as something to “do later”. Later rarely comes, and the AR team ends up as the reporting engine:


- Exporting open items and receipts every Friday
- Rebuilding pivots and charts by hand
- Answering ad hoc questions from the CFO and sales heads
- Producing slightly different numbers each time, depending on who built the report


## Which Accounts Receivable KPIs Matter Most?


There are dozens of possible AR metrics. The following eight cover most of what finance leadership needs.


KPI Formula (simplified) What it tells you


Days sales outstanding (DSO) (Accounts receivable ÷ credit sales) × days in period How long, on average, it takes to collect


Collection effectiveness index (CEI) (Beginning AR + credit sales − ending total AR) ÷ (beginning AR + credit sales − ending current AR) × 100 How much of the collectable balance was actually collected


Collections vs target Actual collections ÷ target collections Whether the team hit the period’s cash goal


Overdue percentage Overdue AR ÷ total AR How much of the book is past due


Aging distribution AR by bucket: current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ Where risk is concentrated


Disputed balance Value and count of invoices in dispute Revenue blocked by issues, not by unwillingness to pay


Promise-to-pay kept rate Promises kept ÷ promises due Quality of collector commitments


Doubtful debt AR over 180 days, or above a provisioning threshold Exposure likely to need provisioning


### DSO


[Days sales outstanding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Days_sales_outstanding) is the most widely used AR metric. It is easy to explain but can be distorted by changes in sales volume. A sales spike at month-end raises DSO even if collections are healthy. Always show the DSO trend, and consider best possible DSO (based only on current receivables) alongside it.


### Collection effectiveness index


CEI measures how well the team collected what was collectable in the period. A CEI close to 100% means almost all collectable receivables were collected. Because CEI is less affected by sales swings than DSO, it is a better measure of collector performance.


### Aging distribution


The[accounts receivable aging report](https://peakflo.co/blog/accounts-receivable-aging-report-analysis-automation) remains essential. In a KPI pack, show it as a distribution over time, so you can see whether balances are moving into older buckets.


## What Should a Weekly Collection Report Include?


The weekly report is an operational tool. It should answer: what came in, what is at risk, and who needs to act?


Section Content


Cash collected this week Total and by entity, country and collector, against weekly target


Month-to-date vs target Running collections against monthly target and predicted collections


Top overdue accounts Largest overdue balances, with owner and next action


Newly overdue Invoices that became overdue this week


Promises due next week Promise-to-pay commitments and their value


Broken promises Promises missed this week, with escalation status


Disputes opened and resolved Count, value and age of disputes


Risk changes Customers that moved up a risk tier


Credit blocks Customers blocked or released this week


## What Should a Monthly Collection Report Include?


The monthly report is for management review. It focuses on trends, performance and exposure.


- **Headline KPIs** : DSO, CEI, overdue percentage and collections vs target, with trends over 6 to 12 months
- **Aging distribution trend** by entity and region
- **Expected vs actual collections bridge** , explaining advances, offsets, adjustments, short payments and non-payment. See[expected vs actual collections variance](https://peakflo.co/blog/expected-vs-actual-collections-variance-reconciliation)
- **Top 20 debtors** with exposure and risk tier
- **Doubtful debt and provisioning movement**
- **Dispute analysis** by root cause, such as pricing, quantity, quality or documentation
- **Team activity** : reminders sent, calls made, tasks completed, promises secured
- **Forecast accuracy** : predicted vs actual collections. See[AI cash flow forecasting from receivables](https://peakflo.co/blog/ai-cash-flow-forecasting-accounts-receivable-predicted-collections)


## How Do Multi-Entity Groups Structure AR Reporting?


Groups with many entities need reporting that works at several levels at once:


- **Entity level** (company code): for local finance managers and statutory needs
- **Country or region level** : for regional commercial heads
- **Division or brand level** : for business unit leaders
- **Group level** : consolidated for the CFO and board


Two practical rules help:


1. **One definition per KPI across the group.** DSO, overdue and CEI must be calculated the same way in every entity, or comparisons are meaningless.
2. **Consistent currency treatment.** Report in local currency for entities and in a group reporting currency for consolidation, with agreed exchange rates.


## Manual vs Automated AR Reporting


Aspect Spreadsheet reporting Automated AR dashboards and reports


Preparation time Hours every week and month Refreshes automatically from ERP


Consistency Varies by preparer One definition for every KPI


Drill-down Rebuild the pivot Click from KPI to customer to invoice


Ad hoc questions New export each time Ask the AI agent in plain language


Entity and region views Separate files Filters on one dataset


Distribution Email attachments Scheduled emails and live dashboards


Freshness As of the export date From near real-time to daily, depending on integration


## How to Set Up Weekly and Monthly AR Reporting


### Step 1: Agree KPI definitions across the group


Write down the formula, data source and period for DSO, CEI, overdue percentage and the other KPIs, and get sign-off from finance leadership.


### Step 2: Integrate AR data from your ERP


Connect open items, receipts, credit notes and customer master data from every company code to your reporting platform.


### Step 3: Add collections activity data


Include reminders, calls, promises to pay, disputes and tasks, so operational KPIs sit next to financial ones.


### Step 4: Build the weekly operational report


Create the weekly view with cash collected, top overdue accounts, promises, broken promises, disputes and risk changes, split by collector.


### Step 5: Build the monthly management pack


Create the monthly view with KPI trends, the aging distribution, the collections bridge, top debtors, doubtful debt and forecast accuracy.


### Step 6: Schedule distribution and enable self-service


Send reports automatically to each audience, and let managers explore the data themselves instead of asking the AR team for exports.

## Our Verdict: Should You Automate Collection Reporting?


Based on how AR teams produce collection reports, here is our view.


### Automate if


- Weekly or monthly collection reports take more than a few hours to build
- You run several entities, countries or divisions
- Leadership regularly asks ad hoc questions the AR team has to answer by hand
- Your ERP project did not include collections reporting


### Spreadsheets may do if


- You have a single entity with a small customer base
- Reporting needs are stable and a single person can maintain the file reliably


**Our Recommendation:** Agree on eight core KPIs, standardise their definitions across the group, and automate both the weekly operational report and the monthly management pack. The aim is that no one on the AR team spends Friday afternoon building reports again.


## Conclusion


Collections reporting is often the gap left behind after an ERP project. The transactions are in the system, but the insight is not. A small set of well-defined KPIs, a weekly report that drives action and a monthly pack that drives review are enough to change how a credit team works.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the most important accounts receivable KPIs?


The core AR KPIs are DSO, collection effectiveness index, collections vs target, overdue percentage, aging distribution, disputed balance, promise-to-pay kept rate and doubtful debt.


### What is the collection effectiveness index?


The collection effectiveness index (CEI) measures the percentage of collectable receivables actually collected in a period. The calculation is (beginning AR + credit sales − ending total AR) divided by (beginning AR + credit sales − ending current AR), multiplied by 100.


### What is the difference between DSO and CEI?


DSO measures the average time to collect and is affected by changes in sales volume. CEI measures how effectively the collectable balance was collected, which makes it a better indicator of collector performance.


### What should a weekly collection report contain?


Cash collected against target, month-to-date progress, top overdue accounts, newly overdue invoices, upcoming and broken promises to pay, dispute movements, risk tier changes and credit blocks.


### What should a monthly AR report contain?


KPI trends, aging distribution, an expected vs actual collections bridge, top debtors, doubtful debt movement, dispute root causes, team activity and forecast accuracy.


### How do you report AR across multiple entities?


Use one KPI definition across the group, report each entity in local currency, consolidate to a group reporting currency, and allow filtering by entity, country and division.


### Why doesn’t our ERP provide collection reports?


ERP implementations focus on transaction processing and statutory reporting. Collections management reporting is often left out of scope and needs either custom development or an AR automation layer.


### What is a doubtful debt KPI?


Doubtful debt is the value of receivables considered at risk of non-collection, often defined as balances over 180 days past due or above a provisioning threshold.


### How often should AR KPIs be reviewed?


Operational KPIs should be reviewed weekly by the credit team, and strategic KPIs monthly by finance leadership, with trends tracked over 6 to 12 months.


### Can AI build AR reports?


Yes. With AR automation platforms like Peakflo, you can describe a report or widget in plain language and the AI agent builds it from your ERP data, ready to publish to a dashboard or export to Excel.
